sources.supports: Tools and environmental feedback form an agent loop; coding agents use tests; stopping conditions and human checkpoints preserve control.

title: The coding-agent feedback loop
summary: Bounded task, tool action, result check and revision or completion.
editorial_guidance: Relevant behavior tests and explicit authorization for consequential production actions are Stackscroll recommendations informed by source principles.
transcript: A coding agent makes progress by checking what its tools did. Start with a bounded task and a clear success condition. Use a tool to inspect code, make an edit, or run a check. Choose tests that check the intended behavior. Read failures, revise the change, and run relevant checks again. Finish when the task is met. Report checks and remaining limits. Ask for authorization before consequential production actions. Confident text is not a passed check.
